Thank you for your service, your commitment to our mokopuna, and your leadership through a period of significant change for our organisation. \n\nYou leave Mana Mokopuna in a strong position to continue advocating for the rights and wellbeing of all children and young people in Aotearoa.\n\nRead the media release on our website: https://bit.ly/4wCNARA","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mana-mokopuna-children-and-young-people-s-commission_today-we-acknowledge-the-significant-contribution-activity-7480785310537199616-rpY8"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Mana Mokopuna | Children's Commissioner","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/mana-mokopuna-children-and-young-people-s-commission"},"datePublished":"2026-07-03T04:30:04.780Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mana-mokopuna-children-and-young-people-s-commission_the-latest-child-poverty-statistics-show-activity-7478666350278774787-AsBB","text":"The latest child poverty statistics show that almost 170,000 children in New Zealand are living in material hardship.\n\nThat's one in seven children going without essentials such as healthy food, adequate heating or visits to the doctor because they are unaffordable for their families.           <p class="break-words text-color-text" data-test-id="about-us__description">
              We are an independent advocate for all 1.2 million children aged under 18 in Aotearoa. We also advocate for care-experienced young people under 25.

Mana Mokopuna - Children and Young People’s Commission is a new name for our organisation, but we have a rich whakapapa built on the commitment of former Children’s Commissioners since 1989.

The Commission is an Independent Crown Entity governed by a board of six Commissioners led by Chief Children’s Commissioner Judge Frances Eivers.

It advocates for children's rights to be recognised and upheld, provides advice and guidance to government and other agencies, advocates for system-level changes, ensures children's voices are heard in decisions that affect them and monitors places where young people are detained.

Our name, Mana Mokopuna, describes who we are and what we stand for.

At its heart, Mana Mokopuna recognises the many elements that support mokopuna to thrive. It focuses on young people in the context of their family, whānau, hapū, iwi and wider community. It also recognises that their participation in decisions that affect them is vitally important.
          </p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Today, we acknowledge the significant contribution of our outgoing Children's Commissioner <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/claire-achmad?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Dr Claire Achmad</a>, whose term ends on 31 July 2026.

Since her appointment as Chief Children's Commissioner in 2023, and as New Zealand's sole Children's Commissioner from 2025, Claire has been a steadfast and independent advocate for the rights, interests, and wellbeing of all 1.2 million mokopuna in Aotearoa.

Claire has always been deeply committed to listening to children and young people directly, ensuring their experiences, aspirations, and concerns inform decision-making at every level. 

Throughout her tenure, Claire has championed children's rights, amplified the voices of children and young people, and consistently called for greater accountability and action on issues that matter most to mokopuna. 

From advocating for improvements in the state care system and implementation of recommendations arising from the Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in State Care, to speaking out on child poverty, maltreatment, barriers to education, mental health, and wellbeing, her leadership has helped keep children's rights at the centre of national conversations.

Ngā manaakitanga, Claire. Thank you for your service, your commitment to our mokopuna, and your leadership through a period of significant change for our organisation. 

You leave Mana Mokopuna in a strong position to continue advocating for the rights and wellbeing of all children and young people in Aotearoa.

Read the media release on our website: <a class="link" href="https://bit.ly/4wCNARA?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>https://bit.ly/4wCNARA</a></p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">The latest child poverty statistics show that almost 170,000 children in New Zealand are living in material hardship.

That's one in seven children going without essentials such as healthy food, adequate heating or visits to the doctor because they are unaffordable for their families. There are now 47,500 more children living in material hardship than there were in 2022.

Against that backdrop, the Healthy School Lunches Programme reaches more than 200,000 children every school day. It is one of the most significant opportunities we have right now to reduce the effects of child poverty, support learning, and ease pressure on family budgets.

In an opinion piece published today in The Post and Waikato Times, Children's Commissioner Dr Claire Achmad reflects on the findings of the Auditor-General's report into the school lunch programme and why we must focus on getting this programme right for the children who rely on it most.

As one of our partners in the oversight of Oranga Tamariki system, Mana Mokopuna works closely with Aroturuki Tamariki.
 
Children’s Commissioner Dr Claire Achmad says the report highlights that too many opportunities are still being missed to prevent mokopuna entering the system — and to ensure their rights are protected when they do.
 
While the majority of mokopuna Māori are not involved with Oranga Tamariki, mokopuna Māori remain disproportionately represented in the system.
 
A key opportunity identified in the report is to build on the successful iwi-led initiatives and strategic partnerships that can be the base for broader long-term change. These help keep mokopuna safe within their whānau.

It aims to ensure young people are part of the conversation as discussions continue around a proposed social media ban for under-16s.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Today we published a new report, 'Children and young people’s perspectives on a safer digital world'.

The report brings forward the views of a diverse group of mokopuna from across Aotearoa New Zealand on digital safety, including the proposed social media ban for under-16s.

The online world is a core part of our children and young people’s lives. Yet their voices have largely been absent from public conversations about online restrictions and safety measures. This report helps bring those perspectives into the discussion.

Mokopuna were clear that that online harm is real and that more must be done to protect their wellbeing. At the same time, they value to positive aspects of being online, including connection, learning, and self-expression. 

Their views reflect the complexity of the issue. While opinions on restrictions were mixed, mokopuna shared thoughtful and practical ideas about how to balance safety with access to online spaces.

As decisions are considered that will directly impact children and young people, it is important that their experiences and perspectives help inform solutions to improve online safety.

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">❤️🖤 Contribute to an Aotearoa New Zealand where all mokopuna live their best lives. Engage your fluency in te reo Māori and your engagement expertise to amplify the experiences of mokopuna and their whānau and communities, ensuring their voices are at the heart of our advocacy.

We are looking for a Kaiarahi to join our new Strategic Communications & Engagement team at Mana Mokopuna – Children’s Commissioner. You will be the kaitiaki of our practice, ensuring every story we tell and every engagement we have honours the inherent mana of mokopuna. 

This is a unique role, leading engagement frameworks grounded in tikanga Māori and international rights conventions. And it's purpose-driven, helping us achieve our moemoeā - Kia kuru pounamu te rongo - All mokopuna live their best lives. 

If you are a fluent te reo Māori speaker and have extensive experience in social or youth work we want to hear from you: <a class="link" href="https://lnkd.in/eNajAgTm?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>https://lnkd.in/eNajAgTm</a></p>
